newsitem.title: USA: Steel imports up this year, will fall in '97-AIIS.
newsitem.headline: Steel imports up this year, will fall in '97-AIIS.

text.p: A stronger-than-expected domestic steel market will push imports this year to higher levels than last year, but some foreign steel will have to find another home as new U.S. supply bumps it out of the market in 1997, an official of the American Institute for International Steel (AIIS) said Monday.
"The (U.S.) market turned around this year," Horst Buelte, AIIS president, told reporters at the trade group's annual meeting. "It was quite a surprise."
The AIIS is a Washington-based trade group that represents nearly 200 steel importers and exporters.
Buelte said total steel imports this year will reach 27.5 million tons, up from last year's total of 24 million tons.
Some industry analysts and executives early this year had predicted that imports would fall below 1995's level.
But mid-year demand from service centers and heavy equipment manufacturers gave the market an unexpected upswing, attracting imports.

"Unquestionably, steel imports helped the U.S. economy maintain its growth momentum," Buelte said. "The steel market this year surprised many of us...instead of continuing to slow down, as had been widely anticipated, it began to gain strength in mid-year."
Buelte also said domestic steel consumption this year will reach in excess of 114 million tons, more than five million tons above last year's level.
Buelte said some foreign steelmakers will have to redirect tonnage next year to other markets as new U.S. supply comes on-stream.
New domestic capacity from upstart minimill companies will add four million tons of supply to the U.S. market by the middle of next year.
"Some imports will suffer as a result of the new capacity," he said. He said imports next year will fall to about 24 to 25 million tons.
But he said markets in Europe and Asia are strengthening, and foreign tonnage that had been coming into the U.S. market could instead find a home there.
He said the overall outlook for the U.S. steel market next year was "uncertain."

"Some observers interpret the recent economic slowdown as the possible end to a seven-year upswing in the U.S. economy and predict a recession for next year. Others see expected global economic expansion, putting upward pressure on international and U.S. steel prices by the middle of the year," he said.
U.S. steelmakers are expected to export less tonnage this year due to the strong home market. Exports should reach about five million tons, down two million tons from last year, Buelte said.
